gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-krub: Pencil-sketched and upright, Blockletter draws every stroke at a single width, like a marker. Krub follows with a tall x-height and curves that lift away before closing, so the two feel like firm lines meeting loose ones.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-kufam: Tubular and tall-bellied, Blockletter looks sketched in pencil without ever leaning on it. Kufam's neon-tube line and open-mouthed e give the pair one steady, glowing quality: every stroke feels drawn with the same unhurried hand.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-lexend: Blockletter's tall midsection bulges like a squat brush-pen belly. Lexend takes over below with oversized lowercase and open-jawed curves, so the heading's sketched weight lands first and the text beneath relaxes into easy, wide-mouthed shapes.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-lexend-deca: Pencil-drawn, tall-bellied and precise: that's Blockletter. Lexend Deca brings an unshaded line, short terminals and big lowercase against small capitals, which is the pair's strongest quality, a heading and body both refusing to fuss or curl.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-liter: Blockletter's bulging midsection looks brush-pen squat but was sketched in pencil, never pressing harder. Liter follows with zero stroke contrast, tall lowercase and wide-mouthed rounds, giving the heading's hand-drawn quirk a straight-edged, upright companion to lean against.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-mada: Mada keeps its curves open and its midzone towering. Blockletter above it has a pipe-cleaner feel in every letterform, so the heading's even, bent-wire strokes and the body's unfinished loops look like cousins drawn with different pens.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-martel-sans: Marker-bold and pencil-sketched, Blockletter looks traced with one nib throughout. Martel Sans follows with generous curve openings and a high mean line, and over a full page those lifted shapes would keep the text feeling spacious.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro opens its c gently and keeps a soft monotone line in a high-waisted lowercase. Maven Pro would take a size nudge upward beside Blockletter's squat, pencil-drawn belly, which already holds its own at any scale.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-michroma: Blockletter's letters read like outlines drawn in one width, tall in the middle and precise. And Michroma gives each letter a wide berth, with open curves and stubby ascenders, so the compact heading and the spacious body trade tension for room.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-miriam-libre: Miriam Libre has the weight of drawn wire and a lowercase with cast-iron stature. And Blockletter, tall-bellied and pencil-sketched, adds a lighter hand above it, so the heading feels penned while the text feels forged.
